chunks.title: The value of a future dollar
chunks.text: It should be obvious now that the value of a dollar delivered in the future, even if it comes from the US government, is worth less than a real dollar right now. A real dollar right now is worth $1. If I promise to give you a dollar in the future, it's not worth as much. So how should we estimate or

chunks.text: think about the value of dollars delivered in the future? I think we've also agreed that the United States government promising to give you a dollar in the future is worth a bit more than the promise of Tucker Balch giving you a dollar in the future. But having a real dollar in your hand right now, this one is worth the most.

chunks.text: Why is that? You know intuitively why that is. The deeper reason is there's a chance that I won't deliver on that guarantee. Whereas we can be pretty sure the US government will deliver on that guarantee. So it amounts to risk.

chunks.title: The value of a future dollar
chunks.text: And it all boils down to interest rate. We're trying to figure out the present value or PV of a dollar that will be delivered in the future. So it's worth some fraction of this future value. Present value is worth some fraction of the future value.

chunks.title: The value of a future dollar
chunks.text: So here's the formula in its entirety. Present value is equal to future value divided by one plus interest rate raised to the I. So the I is how far into the future this payment is going to be delivered. So for instance if it's going to be delivered right now, I is equal to zero, this whole component becomes one and present value is equal simply to future value.

chunks.title: The value of a future dollar
chunks.text: In other words if we're going to pay a dollar, present value is worth one dollar. If in the future that future is going to be one year from now, it's one plus the interest rate raised to the one power and that is what the future value of that dollar is.
